title: Perfectly Spherical Houses in a Vacuum
description: Count how many houses receive at least one present as Santa follows a stream of directions on an infinite grid.
writeup:
## The Puzzle

Santa moves on an infinite 2D grid following a string of `^`, `v`, `<`, `>` characters. He delivers a present at every position he visits (including the start). We need to count distinct houses visited.

## Part 1

Simple coordinate tracking: maintain `(x, y)` and a set of visited positions. Each character maps to a `(dx, dy)` delta. The answer is the size of the visited set.

## Part 2

Now Santa and Robo-Santa alternate: Santa takes the even-indexed moves, Robo-Santa takes the odd-indexed ones, both starting at `(0, 0)`. The neat Python trick here is slice notation:

```python
santa = visited(moves[0::2])  # every other move starting at 0
robo  = visited(moves[1::2])  # every other move starting at 1
```

The answer is the size of the **union** of both visited sets.

## Visualization

The animation replays all three journeys — Santa alone, then Santa's half, then Robo-Santa's half — showing a live viewport that follows the current position and marks every visited house.
